pages.quiz:
INTEGRATED SCIENCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #4
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Milk souring
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Ice melting to water

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Structure of the atom? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Structure of the atom.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Structure of the atom.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Structure of the atom.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structure of the atom.

3. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 37 °C

4. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

5. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Glucose and oxygen

6. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Producers
   D. Decomposers only

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Curved mirrors? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Curved mirrors.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Curved mirrors.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Curved mirrors.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Curved mirrors.

8. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water hardness? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water hardness.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water hardness.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water hardness.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Water hardness.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nutrition in animals? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Nutrition in animals.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition in animals.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutrition in animals.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutrition in animals.

11. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reproduction in plants? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reproduction in plants.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reproduction in plants.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in plants.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Reproduction in plants.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Curved mirrors and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Structure of the atom and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Metals and Alloys and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Water hardness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:

====

2. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structure of the atom.

3. B — 100 °C

4. C — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

5. D — Glucose and oxygen

6. C — Producers

7. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Curved mirrors.

8. D — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

9. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water hardness.

10. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition in animals.

11. D — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

12. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in plants.
